roots.context: We have learned why a spinning top stays up and why weight near the edge keeps it spinning. Now we ask what spinning tells us about ourselves and the world.

deep_truth.truth: Your top spun longer with four coins at its edge than with the same coins at its middle. The coins at the edge raced round a bigger circle on every turn. Faster coins carry more motion, so the rubbing at the tip took longer to use it up. So a turning thing keeps going longest when its weight sits far from its middle.
deep_truth.habit: We usually think of weight as one number: a thing is heavy or light. But the same four coins made the top spin twice as long, or half as long, depending on where they were taped. How a thing moves depends on how its weight is spread, not only on how much there is.
deep_truth.evidence: In the coin top test, the edge top spun clearly longer than the middle top, with the same card, pencil and coins. In the rolling race, a tape roll with its weight at the edge lost to a solid battery.

three.who_am_i: Your head turns to say 'no' on a neck bone that doctors call the axis. You carry a wheel and axle in your own neck.
three.what_is_life: Some bacteria swim by spinning a long thin tail. A tiny motor in their body turns it round, like a wheel on an axle.
three.what_is_this_world: The Earth spins once a day. Its axis slowly circles round like the lean of a top, once in about 26,000 years.

roots.thread: At the middle of every spinning top is a line that does not go round: the axis. Around it, every bit of the top races in its own circle, small near the middle and big at the edge. One still line holds all those different circles together. The many moving parts are one top because they all turn around one middle.

teachings.teaching: Thirty spokes meet at one hub. It is the empty space in the middle that makes the wheel useful.
teachings.link: A wheel's hub is where the axle goes. The middle of a wheel hardly moves, yet the whole wheel turns around it.

teachings.teaching: The wheel of order, with twelve spokes, rolls round the sky and never wears out.
teachings.link: The old poets saw the turning of the year as a wheel. Today we know the Earth itself spins and circles the Sun, and it has kept turning for billions of years because almost nothing in space rubs it to a stop.

teachings.source: The Buddha's first teaching, the Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta (Samyutta Nikaya 56.11)
teachings.teaching: The Buddha's first teaching is called 'setting the wheel of the teaching rolling'. The wheel with 24 spokes on India's flag comes from the same idea, through the Ashoka Chakra.
teachings.link: Once a wheel is set rolling, it keeps going on its own until something slows it. Buridan said the same about a spinning top.

science.text: A spinning thing keeps its spin, and keeps its axis pointing the same way, unless a twisting force changes it. Physicists call this conservation of angular momentum.
Many bacteria swim using a tail turned by a real rotary motor in the outer layers of their cell, one of the smallest motors known.
In 1918 Emmy Noether, a German mathematician, proved that spin is kept because the laws of nature are the same in every direction.

other_view.view: A top stays up because of a law of motion, and there is nothing more to it. The still middle of a wheel is a fact of geometry. Reading a lesson about oneness into it says more about us than about tops.

practice.title: Watch the still middle
practice.say: Let's spin our top on the plate and sit very still. Look only at the very top of the pencil. Everything else is a blur, but the middle hardly moves. Breathe in slowly as it spins. Breathe out slowly. Keep watching until it wobbles and falls. Then sit still for three more breaths.
practice.kid: Spin your top. Look only at the top of the pencil. Breathe in slowly. Breathe out slowly. Watch until it falls. Then sit still for three breaths.

playtest: Every experiment, activity, game, challenge and project was walked through as if at home today, with the materials listed. The coin top needs stiff card: thin cereal-box card bends under the coins, so the step asks for a shoebox lid or two glued layers. An off-centre pencil makes any top fall in a few seconds, so the step shows how to find the middle by folding a paper circle. The edge-or-middle result needs fair spins: the step asks for 3 spins each, and for 3 more if the times are close. The rolling race uses a tape roll and an AA battery, both found in most homes, and a metal or plastic bangle, never glass. The dupatta merry-go-round is walked slowly, with furniture moved away. The chair-swing ride needs a pencil that turns freely in the bottle mouth. The coin spin may give 0 seconds on a towel, which the step calls a real result. how_we_found_out.story: For about two thousand years, many teachers in Europe and the Middle East followed Aristotle, a Greek thinker. He taught that a moving thing needs something pushing it all the time. So why does a thrown stone keep flying after it leaves your hand? Many of his followers said the air rushes round behind it and pushes it along. Around 1350, Jean Buridan, a teacher at the University of Paris, asked a simple question about a spinning top and a smith's grinding wheel. Both keep turning for a long time after the push. Yet neither one moves from its place. There is no gap behind them for air to rush into. So the air cannot be what keeps them going. Buridan said the push puts something into the moving thing itself. He called it impetus. He said it would last for ever, if the air and the rubbing did not slowly take it away. About 300 years later, Isaac Newton made this into his first law of motion: a moving thing keeps moving until a force changes it.
how_we_found_out.who: Jean Buridan, a French teacher at the University of Paris, and later Isaac Newton, an English scientist
how_we_found_out.wrong_idea: People thought moving things need a push all the time, and that the air pushes a thrown stone along. Buridan pointed out that a spinning top keeps turning in one place, where air cannot rush in behind it. So the motion must be carried by the top itself.
